unite_adi: REGULAR UPPER SECONDARY-YEAR 9-LEVEL: B1.1 - THEME 6: LIFE IN THE CITY & COUNTRY

bolumler.ogrenmeKanitlari: PERFORMANCE ASSIGNMENT: Students prepare a self-recording (visual, audio) at school/ at home, conducting an interview with classmates about ''local and international festivals which are held in the city, different kinds of food produced for such festivals, and local and international food culture'' and present it to the class and receiving feedback about it. They can also write and design the content of a ''food festival'' programme content and then they present and apply it as an acting out activity by inviting other students as visitors or food presenters to the festival in class to present different food cultures, cuisines, dishes etc. The assignment will be evaluated by using rubrics. Öğrenme-Öğretme Yaşantıları
bolumler.temelKabuller: This theme is based on the concept of ''local and international festivals which are held in the city, different kinds of food produced for such festivals, and local and international food culture'' in English. As they are upper secondary students in Year 9, they are expected to know what food is and what a local food is in their own language. They are also aware that almost all people, although there are exceptions, would know different types of food, the food types served in festivals, local and international food types and food cultures from different parts of the world. Students can think about and express such situations in their own languages, but they may not know how to say them in a foreign language if they have not been covered at all or only partially covered in their existing curriculum. However, this existing knowledge in their own language would prepare them to identify the same concepts later and help them recognise, understand, and learn the new information about the new concept and theme more easily in their foreign language, English. In terms of preparation for the current new theme, it is assumed that they have learnt basic types of food such as ''fish, chicken, eggs, bread, milk, water, fruits (tomatoes, apples, oranges, bananas), vegetables (potatoes, carrots, beans), fast food (unhealthy food) (hamburgers, spaghetti, sausages)'', how to ask what things are by using language chunks such as ''What’s/is it/this? What are they?'' how to ask for permission or possibility by using language chunks such as ''Can I……?'', how to ask and answer whether some food exists by using ''Is there/are there…? There’s/is and There are'', how to descriptive food by using adjectives such as ''good, bad, nice, yummy'', and how to ask and answer about the amount of food with quantity words such as ''how much, how many, some, any, much, many'' and by using grammatical structures that practise Simple Present Tense and Present Progressive in English from the previous themes or years. These language items and vocabulary can be used as a basis for learning the new language grammar items in use in the current theme, making the new ones in the current theme easier to learn.
bolumler.onDegerlendirme: It is expected that the physical, cognitive, affective, and social factors are appropriate and suitable for students to learn about ''local and international festivals which are held in the city, different kinds of food produced for such festivals, and local and international food culture''. A short contextual written story about food for remembering and practising the previously learnt items could be delivered to students to discuss and fill in the blanks with the required words in pairs. This session can help them revise all these vocabulary and language grammar items in use from previous themes or previous years as a preparatory practice. In this way, their performance can be evaluated in terms of how much they remember and how much these items are used correctly to be able to build their competence in the current theme. It can help the teacher decide what to emphasise or practise for revising the previous knowledge and to facilitate the new vocabulary and grammar items in use in the current theme.
bolumler.zenginlestirme: Objective: To talk about different kinds of food produced for local and international festivals and food culture in English by using target vocabulary and target grammar. Activity 1: Festival Organisers and Visitors Role-Play The teacher divides students into two groups: Festival Organisers and Visitors. Each organiser group is assigned a specific festival (e.g., Adana Orange Flower Festival, French Omelette Festival, Spanish Taco Festival) and prepares key information, such as the festival’s location, food served, and activities. Organisers set up a ''festival booth'' to promote their event, while visitor groups rotate among the booths, asking questions like, ''What kind of food do you serve?'', ''What are you making/cooking?'' or ''Is this a local or international festival?''. Organisers respond fluently, using target vocabulary and language functions. After one round, the groups switch roles, so all students practise both presenting and questioning skills. The teacher and students provide feedback on vocabulary use and pronunciation. At the end of the activity, students prepare a poster about the festival they presented and display it on the class notice board. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity. Objective: To describe local and international food festivals and food culture in English by using target vocabulary and target grammar. Activity 2: Festival Information Gap-Fill Listening Activity The teacher prepares short audio clips describing different festivals and foods (e.g., ''In Japan, the Ramen Festival offers a variety of noodle dishes. Chefs prepare bowls of ramen with broth, vegetables, and chicken, and egg toppings'') and upload them to a web tool to create a listening gap-fill exercise. Students listen to the audio clips and complete the missing information directly on the web tool (e.g., ''The Festival offers a variety of noodle dishes''). They then record themselves using an audio recording tool, repeating the sentences fluently. The teacher plays some of the recordings in class and provides feedback on pronunciation and sentence accuracy, while students also give peer feedback to improve their speaking skills. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
bolumler.destekleme: Objective: To describe different kinds of food produced for local and international festivals and food culture in English by using target vocabulary and target grammar. Activity 1: Festival Food Matching Game The teacher gives students cards in two different categories: food items in the first category and festivals in the second. Students work in pairs, and each pair receives the cards. They match each food with the relevant festival. (e.g., Adana Orange Flower Festival – orange jam) After completing the matching, students create simple sentences based on examples shown on the board, such as: ''This is a local festival. They make orange jam at the Adana Orange Flower Festival''. The teacher encourages students to say their sentences aloud, helping them practise pronunciation. The pair that completes the correct matches the fastest and creates accurate sentences wins the activity. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity. Objective: To help students recognise and identify local and international festivals and food culture in English by using target vocabulary and target grammar. Activity 2: Festival Food Listening Activity The teacher prepares short audio clips describing different festivals and food (e.g., ''In France, at the Omelette Festival, they cook a large omelette in a big pan'') and uploads them to a web tool to create a listening quiz. Students listen to the audio clips and select the correct answer from multiple-choice options with the corresponding festival or food item (e.g., Omelette Festival – Omelette). After completing the listening part, students work in pairs to practise the sentences from the audio and record themselves using an audio recording tool, repeating the target sentences. The teacher plays some of the recordings and provides feedback on pronunciation and sentence accuracy, while students also give peer feedback. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
